key_insight: DemoPSD shows that policy self-distillation can be improved by modulating teacher guidance with disagreement signals, rather than relying on dense token-level supervision alone. This helps reduce overfitting and preserve exploration, improving generalization beyond the training domain.
problem_solved: The paper addresses a core limitation of on-policy self-distillation for LLM reasoning: privileged teacher supervision can become too rigid, causing the student to overfit to in-domain patterns, explore less, and generalize poorly across domains.
method: Uses a single model in a teacher-student setup with different information access, following the on-policy self-distillation paradigm.
Introduces disagreement modulation to control when and how strongly teacher signals are applied during training.
Reduces reliance on dense token-level supervision so the student can maintain exploration while still learning useful reasoning behavior.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a more robust way to train reasoning LLMs without sacrificing cross-domain performance. It is especially relevant for settings where generalization, stability, and exploration matter more than fitting in-domain patterns.
visual_elements: Split teacher-student pipeline diagram showing privileged vs. non-privileged information
Before/after comparison chart of standard OPSD vs. DemoPSD on generalization and overfitting

Icon set for exploration, overfitting, and cross-domain transfer
paper_authors: Yunhe Li, Hao Shi, Wenhao Liu, Mengzhe Ruan, Hanxu Hou
